title: The Bottle Without a Message
skyStory: Fifty-six percent of moon floats in Pisces for one last night, and the sea has sent a bottle up the beach with nothing inside. No note. No map. Just a bottle and a sense of possibility. Pisces holds it up to the moonlight. The moon says the message is whatever you put in it. Saturn mutters something about recycling.

reading: There is an empty bottle in your life today: a gap, a cleared afternoon, a quiet hour that was supposed to be busy. The Tiger wants to fill it immediately. Do not. Look at it first.

The waning moon is about releasing, and this empty space is a gift. Put one thing into it on purpose: a nap, a walk, a phone call, a page of writing. Just one. [[The Hanged Man]] is hanging upside down in the corner, grinning, because a new angle always shows up when you stop rushing to fill every gap.
joel.mission: Leave one empty hour today completely unscheduled, then choose a single thing to put in it at the last minute.
joel.omen: An empty bench, chair or bottle. Space is opening for something gentle; leave room for it.

reading: A bottle washes up at your feet, and it is empty. The Wood Rat inspects it thoroughly, sniffs it, holds it to the light. Nothing. Then the realisation: you are meant to write the message.

Write a note to yourself six months from now, to the woman who will be standing in the long dark of her solstice birthday. Tell her what this summer was like. Seal it somewhere safe. Release the rest of today's small worries into the outgoing tide, one by one. They do not need a bottle. They can swim.
nancy.mission: Write a short note to your December self about this summer, seal it in an envelope and tape it inside the cover of a winter book.
nancy.omen: Sea glass on the beach or a coloured stone. A small surprise from the past is on its way.
nancy.stoneWhy: Joel's fire, sealed in the bottle

together.text: Message in a bottle. Each of you writes one sentence you want to send to the other six months from now. Save it in a note titled Bottle. On December 22, Nancy's birthday, you both open your notes and read them out loud together.
